quote: 1. With every trade I make, my approach is always 'risk-first.' By thinking and acting 'risk-first,' you know exactly what you stand to lose if you're wrong, which in trading is far more important than what you stand to gain if you're right, because if you lose all your chips, the game is over.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 2. I believe that good investors are successful not because of their IQ, but because they have an investing discipline.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 3. The main thing is that you cut your loss immediately, without any vacillation.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 4. You don't have to involve yourself in every market movement. In fact, you should not attempt to. Be an exacting opportunist. Be selective and pick your entry spots very carefully. Wait until the probabilities are stacked in your favor before you act. With patience and discipline, you can profit from market opponents who are less disciplined and less capable than you are.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 5. Success in investing doesn't correlate with I.Q. once you're above the level of 125. Once you have ordinary intelligence, what you need is the temperament to control the urges that get other people into trouble in investing.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 6. If you're early on in your career and they give you a choice between a great mentor or higher pay, take the mentor every time. It's not even close. And don't even think about leaving that mentor until your learning curve peaks.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 7. I've never made a buy at a low that I didn't just feel terrible and scared to death making it. It's easy to sell at the bottom. You can go home that night and it relieves you of your nerves. When things are going down it's hard to buy them.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 8. During the consolidation phase, decreasing volume is good. If you continue to see very high volume, it is a potential top because it shows that a lot of people are getting out of the stock.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 9. The wonderful thing about our business is that it's liquid, and you can wipe the slate clean on any day.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 10. Letting losses run is the most serious mistake made by most investors.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 11. Never let a big winner turn into a loser.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 12. Never invest in the present. It's the anticipation of future earnings that moves stocks.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 13. I bought $6 billion worth of tech stocks and in six weeks I had lost $3 billion.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 14. Average up, not down.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 15. Buy stocks that are making new highs, not stocks that are making new lows.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 16. Amateurs think about how much they can make; professionals think about how much they can lose.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 17. Put all your eggs in one basket and then watch the basket very carefully.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 18. Cut your losses short and let your winners run.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 19. Don't try to catch a falling knife; let the stock prove itself before you buy.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 20. I look for the strongest stocks in the strongest industry groups.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 21. When the facts change, I change my position quickly; the market doesn't care what I thought yesterday.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 22. The mistake I'd say 98 percent of money managers and individuals make is they feel like they've got to be playing with a bunch of stuff.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 23. If you don't feel like a fool, you're not managing risk.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 24. I studied historical models of great winning stocks to ingrain in my mind what a stock looked like before it made a major move. I tried to get to the point where I was looking at the exact same things O'Neil did. He was my role model.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 25. Virtually every superperformance phase in big, winning stocks occurred while the stock price was in a definite price uptrend. In almost every case, the trend was identifiable early in the superperformance advance.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 26. The only reason you can change your mind is if you're not arrogant about a position.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 27. Do not, do NOT invest in the present; the present is not what moves stock prices, change does.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 28. Your first loss is your best loss.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 29. I don't ever want to own a stock that is not working for me; if it isn't acting right, I get out.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 30. What I'm trying to do is discount what the world will look like 18 months from now, not what it looks like today.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 31. I've always loved to play games, and face it: investing is one big game. You need to be decisive, open-minded, flexible and competitive.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 32. Always think about risk in relation to reward, and adjust your risk as a function of the potential reward.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 33. Keep your losses small, admit your mistakes, and move on to the next stock.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 34. Having strong convictions is vital, but incredibly important is the ability to change your mind.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 35. It's not the big loss that kills you; it's the failure to cut the small one.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 36. The strongest stocks tend to get stronger; buy relative strength and let the market confirm your idea.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 37. I like the concentrated bets. I like the fat pitches and the swing big. And I also like it when you don't see a fat pitch, stand there, and let the pitches go by.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 38. Growth comes at the expense of comfort.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 39. The most comprehensive work I have ever read on investing in growth stocks.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 40. I've learned that when you have tremendous conviction on a trade, you have to go for the jugular. It takes courage to be a pig.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 41. Buy high and sell higher; the best stocks are the ones already showing strength.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 42. I always sell a stock if it drops 7 or 8 percent below my purchase price.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 43. I've never used valuation to time the market. Valuation only tells you how far something can go once a catalyst is in place.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 44. Only buy stocks in a Stage 2 uptrend, and never buy a stock in a Stage 4 decline.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 45. I like to buy stocks as they break out of a base to new highs on heavy volume.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 46. Limit your risk on any single trade to 1.25% to 2.5% of your capital.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 47. The first priority is to preserve capital; you can't make money if you're out of the game.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 48. I never fall in love with a stock; when it breaks my rules, I sell it.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 49. Earnings don't move the overall market; it's the Federal Reserve Board. Focus on the central banks and focus on the movement of liquidity.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 50. Even if you're right only half the time, you can make good money as long as your average gain is at least twice your average loss.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 51. A good stock acts right from the day you buy it; if it hangs around your buy point and doesn't move, I get out.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 52. Position sizing is what separates survivors from casualties; size up only when the evidence and the tape agree.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 53. The trend is your friend until liquidity says otherwise; watch what the central banks do, not what companies say.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 54. Watch the leaders: when the best stocks stop going up on good news, the market is telling you something.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 55. The way to build long-term returns is through preservation of capital and home runs.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 56. A 50% loss requires a 100% gain just to get back to even.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 57. I look for stocks with the best earnings growth and relative strength, and buy them when they break out of a proper base.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 58. Soros has taught me that when you have tremendous conviction on a trade, you have to go for the jugular.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 59. Knowing what not to buy is as important as knowing what to buy.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 60. I'm not afraid to be wrong, but I'm afraid to stay wrong.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 61. It's not whether you're right or wrong that's important, but how much money you make when you're right and how much you lose when you're wrong.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 62. Your objective is not to be right, but to make money.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 63. The big money is made by holding on to the few big winners.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 64. The ability to admit mistakes quickly is paramount.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 65. Sometimes the best trade is no trade at all.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 66. It's just a matter of figuring out which stocks are going to be leaders and buying them early in the move.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 67. The greatest investors make large concentrated bets where they have a lot of conviction. They're not buying 35 or 40 names and diversifying.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 68. To compound your capital rapidly, you must be where the action is.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 69. It's more important to make money than it is to be right.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 70. Soros doesn't give a damn about where he got in. That was the most important lesson I learned from him.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 71. You don't have to be right all the time to be successful; you have to keep your losses small.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 72. I'd rather pay up for a stock that is proven strong than buy a cheap one that isn't working.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 73. Bulls make money, bears make money, and pigs get slaughtered. I'm here to tell you I was a pig a lot of times.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 74. Never average down.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 75. I only buy a stock when it is showing me it's right.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 76. The first thing I heard when I got in the business, from a very smart man, was 'Bulls make money, bears make money, and pigs get slaughtered.'
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 77. Cash is a position.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 78. The market is the best indicator; the leaders will tell you what is going on.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 79. It's not what you make on your winners, but what you give back on your losers that determines success.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 80. You have to be flexible, and when you're wrong, get out. Pride is the enemy.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 81. I try to find stocks that are doing something right now, with strong earnings and strong price action.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 82. It's better to lose correctly than to win incorrectly.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 83. There is no intelligent reason to increase your trading size if your positions are showing losses.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 84. You can be far more aggressive when you're making good profits.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 85. If something needs to be hedged, you shouldn't have a position in it.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 86. To compound your money, and not your mistakes, your goal is to buy on the way up—not on the way down.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 87. Both opportunity and perils surface suddenly in the market.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 88. A stock doesn't know you own it.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 89. Price and volume tell you everything you need to know about a stock.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 90. What matters is the direction of change, not the level.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
